rationale: Water damage to the policyholder's own basement, flooring, drywall, and contents caused by a burst supply line in their own plumbing is direct property damage covered under homeowners insurance.
claim_summary: Sam Patel (POL-1004) returned home from a work trip to find the basement flooded with approximately two inches of water. The damage is extensive: hardwood flooring throughout the basement is buckled, drywall is soaked up to one foot high, and numerous stored boxes are ruined. The cause was a burst supply line in the policyholder's own plumbing. With a $500 deductible and $750,000 coverage limit, this high-severity property damage claim requires immediate adjuster assessment for water extraction, structural drying, flooring replacement, drywall repair, and contents restoration.

case_facts.items_affected: Hardwood flooring buckled, drywall soaked up to one foot high, stored boxes ruined
case_facts.cause: Burst supply line in policyholder's plumbing

rationale: Wind damage to the policyholder's own roof shingles is straightforward property damage to the insured dwelling.
claim_summary: Jordan Lee (POL-1006) reported wind damage to four roof shingles on the back porch overhang from last weekend. No interior water damage or structural issues. Estimated repair cost is $400 to replace shingles. Policy is active with $2,500 deductible and $1M coverage limit. This is a low-severity property damage claim requiring roofing contractor assessment.

case_facts.description: four shingles blown off by wind; no interior damage or water intrusion
